skill.name: global-commenting
skill.description: Write minimal, evergreen comments for code that needs explanation. Use it for PHPDoc, JSDoc, TSDoc, comment reviews, and self-documenting code decisions.
skill.summary: Guides AI assistants to add durable comments only where they clarify non-obvious code.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: The static path traversal alert is a fixed Markdown link to a project standards document, not executable code or user-controlled file access. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The skill links to a standards file outside the packaged skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Inline the required commenting guidance or include the referenced standards file inside the skill package.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 26 is a fixed Markdown reference to a project standards document, not dynamic filesystem access. The target path is not a sensitive file and no user input can alter the path.

content.value_statement: Teams often add comments that become stale or repeat obvious code. This skill guides AI assistants to write minimal comments that explain non-obvious decisions.
actual_capabilities: Guides comments for PHP, TypeScript, JavaScript, and other code files.
Supports PHPDoc blocks for PHP classes, methods, and functions.
Supports JSDoc and TSDoc comments for TypeScript and JavaScript functions.
Encourages comments that explain non-obvious business logic and algorithms.
Helps review existing comments for relevance and long-term accuracy.
Promotes clearer naming and structure before adding comments.
limitations: The packaged skill does not include the detailed external commenting standard.
The linked standards file may be unavailable after marketplace installation.
It provides writing guidance, not automated linting or enforcement.
It does not replace project-specific documentation rules.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Code Comments
use_cases.description: Review comments in a codebase and keep only those that explain lasting context.

use_cases.title: Standardize Docblocks
use_cases.description: Create PHPDoc, JSDoc, or TSDoc comments that match a minimal commenting style.

use_cases.title: Reduce Comment Noise
use_cases.description: Identify comments that repeat code behavior and suggest clearer naming or structure.

prompt_templates.title: Add Essential Comments
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small file or function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code and add only comments that explain non-obvious decisions. Avoid comments that repeat what the code already says.

prompt_templates.title: Write Docblocks
prompt_templates.prompt: Add PHPDoc, JSDoc, or TSDoc comments where they help future maintainers. Keep each comment concise and focused on intent.

prompt_templates.title: Review Comment Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Cleaning up comments during a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing comments in this change. Mark stale, redundant, or temporary comments, and suggest durable replacements only where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Before Commenting
prompt_templates.prompt: Find places where clearer names or structure would remove the need for comments. Add comments only for business rules or algorithms that remain non-obvious.

output_examples.input: A service method contains several comments that restate each assignment and condition.
output_examples.output: The review removes redundant comments and keeps one short note explaining the business rule behind the condition.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript function has complex date logic with no context.
output_examples.output: The result adds a concise TSDoc summary and one inline comment explaining the calendar rule.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds comments about a temporary migration workaround.
output_examples.output: The review suggests removing time-bound wording and documenting the stable reason for the compatibility check.

best_practices: Explain why code exists when the reason is not clear from names and structure.
Prefer clearer code before adding a comment.
Keep comments durable by avoiding release dates, temporary notes, and recent-change history.
anti_patterns: Do not comment every line or repeat obvious control flow.
Do not preserve stale comments after logic changes.
Do not use comments to hide unclear naming or overly complex structure.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants write fewer, better code comments that explain non-obvious intent.

faq.question: Which languages does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions PHP, TypeScript, JavaScript, PHPDoc, JSDoc, and TSDoc.

faq.question: Does it generate complete documentation?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on code comments and docblocks, not full project documentation.

faq.question: Can it remove comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide removal of stale, redundant, or temporary comments.

faq.question: Does it enforce style automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for an AI assistant and does not run a linter.

faq.question: Is the detailed standard included?
faq.answer: No. The skill links to a standards file outside the packaged skill directory.
